terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation; with the dative
evidence: Publ. N 5: Nūllus est tam tūtus quaestus, quam quod habeās parcere.
Cic. Fam. 16.4.2: tē rogō sūmptū nē parcās ūllā in rē
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to act sparingly, be sparing with respect to a thing”: to spend less is to be sparing with expense (sūmptū parcere). Publilius has the older accusative. Thrifty is frūgī or frūgālis (Traupman 158).

evidence: Ter. Ph. 43–44: quod ille ūnciātim vix dē dēmēnsō suō, suum dēfrūdāns genium, comparsit miser
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to save, husband well, lay up (ante- and post-class.)”; it quotes Terence’s line with the reading compersit.

evidence: Verg. E. 1.32: nec spēs lībertātis erat, nec cūra pecūlī
terms.comment: Classically the money a slave or a son was allowed to keep as his own; Traupman’s savings bank is argentāria pecūliīs asservandīs.

evidence: Plaut. Pers. 471: ego hodiē compendī fēcī bīnōs pānēs in diēs
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: compendium, “a saving or gain, profit acquired by saving (opp. dispendium)”.

phrases.latin: Nūllus est tam tūtus quaestus, quam quod habeās parcere.
phrases.english: There is no profit as safe as saving what you have.

phrases.latin: quod ille ūnciātim vix dē dēmēnsō suō, suum dēfrūdāns genium, comparsit miser
phrases.english: what the poor fellow has scraped together, ounce by ounce, out of his monthly ration, cheating himself of every pleasure

phrases.latin: nec spēs lībertātis erat, nec cūra pecūlī
phrases.english: I had no hope of freedom, and no thought of savings.

sources: Lewis & Short: parco · Lewis & Short: comparco · Lewis & Short: peculium · Lewis & Short: compendium
